title: Investigating Stress-relaxation and Failure Responses in the Trachea
protocol: Acquire a cadaver of a pig from an approved farm.
Keep the cadaver on ice until tissue harvest is completed.
Place the cadaver in the supine position.
Make a vertical midline incision along the neck.
Expose the thyroid cartilage, cricoid cartilage, and trachea from the hyoid bone to the suprasternal notch.
Harvest the larynx and full-length trachea using a #10 blade.
Separate the trachea sample from the larynx.
Cut the tracheal tube longitudinally along the entire length on one side using the #10 blade.
Measure the thickness of the trachea using an acquired cross-sectional image.
Cut the trachea into two circumferential strips approximately 5 mm wide proximally.
Cut the trachea into two longitudinal strips approximately 5 mm wide distally.
Ensure each strip is at least 25 mm long.
Obtain images of the four cut trachea strips alongside a ruler.
Use Image J to provide digitized measurements of the sample width from the images.
Calculate the cross-sectional area using measured width during data analysis.
Keep all tissue samples hydrated with sterile phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) solution throughout the study.
Hydrate the tissue in PBS just before testing for proper hydration.
Attach each sample longitudinally between custom-designed clamps without inducing any stretch.
Fix the clamps to a material testing machine with a 50 N load cell attached to the top actuator.
Measure the grip-to-grip distance using a ruler.
Use measured grip-to-grip distance as the initial tissue length for strain calculations.
Perform preconditioning by tensile loading each sample five times at a 1%/s strain rate to 1% strain.
Hold each sample at peak elongation of 0% or 10% for 300 seconds.
Post the stress-relaxation test, stretch the tissue immediately at 1%/s until mechanical failure occurs.
Document the failure site.
Confirm no slip has occurred by ensuring the presence of samples within the clamps post testing.
Record the stress-relaxation and failure testing videos using a digital camera at a minimum of 30 frames/s.
Acquire time (s), load (N), and displacement (mm) data using a data acquisition software at a sampling rate of 250 samples/s during both stress-relaxation and failure testing.
Save the acquired data as a .csv file for data analysis.
Acquire still images of the clamped tissue before stress-relaxation, after stress-relaxation, and after failure.
Download and install MATLAB data analysis software, including the "Optimization" and "Image Processing" toolboxes.
Navigate to the downloaded zipped folder containing the MATLAB codes and sample dataset.
Extract the contents of the downloaded zipped folder.
Open MATLAB and set the unzipped folder as the working directory.
Navigate to the Failure Only folder.
Store data from samples tested on a particular date in one Microsoft Excel file using the mmddyy naming convention.
Open Failure Only | 043022.xlsx.
Label samples using the convention [sample type]_[sample number]_[insert pre-stretch strain level]%.
For example, name control group tracheal samples as TA_1_0% and TC_1_0%, where 0% denotes no pre-stretch.
Name experimental group tracheal samples as TA_1_10% and TC_1_10%, reflecting 10% pre-stretch under axial or circumferential loading conditions before mechanical failure testing.
Select the worksheet tab named TA_1_0%.
Label raw data header columns exactly as follows: Time (sec), Load (N), Position (mm), Diameters (mm), Average Cross-sectional Area (Thickness x Width, mm²), Initial Length (mm).
Close the current Microsoft Excel file titled Failure Only | 043022.xlsx.
Return to the working directory of the data analysis software.
Navigate to the Relaxation folder.
Store experimental group biomechanical data in one Microsoft Excel file using the mmddyy labeling convention.
Open Relaxation | 043022.xlsx and toggle through each worksheet tab containing raw load relaxation data from samples tested on April 30th, 2022.
Ensure that the raw load relaxation data for each sample are formatted correctly.
Save and close the current Microsoft Excel file, Relaxation | 043022.xlsx.
Return to the working directory of the data analysis software.
Navigate to the folder Failure (Post-Relaxation).
Open the Microsoft Excel file Failure (Post-Relaxation) | 043022.xlsx.
Recognize multiple worksheet tabs containing raw mechanical failure data from tracheal samples.
Ensure that sample labels match those in Relaxation | 043022.xlsx.
Toggle through each worksheet tab to ensure header columns are formatted correctly.
Close the current Microsoft Excel file, Failure (Post-Relaxation) | 043022.xlsx.
Return to the working directory of the data analysis software.
Repeat steps 4.1.5-4.1.26 for additional testing dates as applicable.
Open the Microsoft Excel file, testingDates.xlsx.
List testing dates in the first column in mm/dd/yy format.
Indicate with a Y or N whether samples on this date were from the experimental group.
Indicate with a Y or N whether samples on this date were from the control group.
Repeat steps 4.1.29-4.1.31 for additional testing dates as applicable.
Save and close the current Microsoft Excel file, testingDates.xlsx.
Return to the working directory of the data analysis software.
Open the main script file, main_relax_failure.m.
Select the large, green arrow on the software interface to run the code.
Alternatively, type run main_calc_relax in the command window.
Upon being prompted, input comma-separated fixed elongation levels (in %) for the various experimental groups and press OK.
Input comma-separated stress-relaxation testing durations for the various experimental groups in seconds and press OK.
Hold tracheal samples at fixed elongation for 300 s for stress relaxation response testing.
Convert load-time data to nominal stress-time data using main_relax_failure.m code.
Determine peak load and stress magnitudes in response to the application of the 10% fixed elongation on the sample.
Calculate the percentage reduction in stress at 300 s using the specified equation.
Model the viscoelastic stress relaxation response using a two-term Prony series exponential decay model.
Normalize calculated stress values to produce a reduced relaxation function.
Curve-fit G(t) using nonlinear least-squares regression.
Use code main_relax_failure.m to convert load-displacement data to nominal stress-strain data.
Apply equations for nominal stress σ = F / A0, where F is circumferential or axial load and A0 is initial cross-sectional area.
Apply equations for resultant strain ε = ΔL / L0, where ΔL is displacement and L0 is the sample's initial length.
Consider pre-stretched length as L0 for samples subjected to failure tensile testing following stress relaxation hold.
Identify maximum load (failure load) and corresponding failure displacement using calc_relax_failure.m function.
Determine maximum stress (failure stress) and corresponding failure strain using calc_relax_failure.m function.
Discard load-displacement data following the failure load using calc_relax_failure.m function.
Use function (calc_relax_failure.m) to plot the load-displacement curve.
Manually select two points in the linear region of the curve to approximate tissue stiffness.
Utilize selected x- and y-coordinates from the load-displacement curve to compute the modulus of elasticity.
Repeat step for every sample.
Ensure computed results are saved as a Microsoft Excel file in the working directory with naming convention relax_failure_results_mmddyy.xlsx.
